lead.t: Skin lesions: “Do you have pustular or scaly rash on palms/soles, or nail changes?” — Psoriatic arthritis is associated with psoriasis; nail pitting or onycholysis are clues.

| Psoriatic arthritis | Skin psoriasis, nail pitting, dactylitis, asymmetric oligo/polyarthritis | Presence of skin lesions, distal interphalangeal joint involvement, negative RF/anti‑CCP |
*Psoriatic arthritis* – asymmetric oligo‑/polyarthritis, skin plaques, nail pitting.
The umbrella includes ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, reactive arthritis, enteropathic arthritis and undifferentiated spondyloarthritis.
Inflammatory arthritis: pseudogout, rheumatoid arthritis, seronegative spondyloarthropathy(reactive arthritis, psoriatic arthritis)

qs.q: A 45-year-old woman with chronic plaque psoriasis develops asymmetric arthritis affecting her distal interphalangeal joints and sausage-like swelling of her digits. Which radiographic finding is characteristic of advanced psoriatic arthritis?
o: Pencil‑in‑cup appearance resulting from marked marginal bone erosion.
Widespread periarticular osteopenia while joint spaces remain intact.
Symmetric joint space narrowing accompanied by large subchondral cysts.
Bridging syndesmophytes linking adjacent lumbar vertebrae.
Calcification within hyaline cartilage (chondrocalcinosis) of the knee.
qs.e: Psoriatic arthritis features distinct radiographic changes including the classic 'pencil-in-cup' deformity from bone lysis.
